structure.heading: Macro Environment Outlook and Implications for Cost of Capital, Demand, and Risk
text_content: **Macro Environment Outlook and Implications for Cost of Capital, Demand, and Risk**

Base-case 2026 outlook assumes global GDP growth of 2.6% and CPI inflation of 3.1%. This baseline, aligned with recent IMF and OECD projections, implies a modest expansion environment where real demand growth is heterogenous across regions: stronger services-led consumption in the United States and UK, muted manufacturing investment in the Eurozone and China, and selective strength in commodity exporters. For demand planning this means conservative topline assumptions are prudent, with higher pass-through of consumer prices into volumes in lower-income markets. Central bank normalization trajectories remain varied, raising expectations of policy rate differentials that will persist through FY2026 and influence cross-border capital flows and corporate borrowing costs. Forecast uncertainty remains elevated into 2027.

The planning WACC increased from 8.2% in FY2024 to 10.1% for FY2026 portfolio decisions. This step-change in the weighted average cost of capital materially raises discount rates used in valuation, reduces net present values, and increases the minimum acceptable internal rates of return for new investments. Capital allocation frameworks must therefore be recalibrated to reflect higher hurdle rates, with priority given to projects demonstrating resilient cash conversion, shorter payback periods, and protected margins. Treasury and corporate finance should update capital structure targets, review covenant headroom, and stress-test debt servicing under scenario-specific rates, ensuring liquidity buffers are maintained for adverse outcomes and funding plans are confirmed for FY2026–FY2028. This is non-negotiable operational discipline.

sections.heading: Macroeconomic Environment Update
sections.body: Global growth forecasts for FY2026 have been revised downward to 2.3%, with continued weakness in European industrial output and moderating demand in North America. Central bank policy rates remain elevated, with our weighted average borrowing cost increasing from 4.1% to 6.2% over the past eighteen months. Input cost inflation has moderated but remains above pre-2022 levels, particularly in logistics and skilled labor. These conditions necessitate a disciplined capital allocation framework prioritizing liquidity, margin resilience, and returns above our revised 11% hurdle rate.

sections.heading: Portfolio Performance Overview
sections.body: Core Infrastructure Services delivered $412M in EBITDA for Q1 2026, up 3% year-over-year, supported by long-term contracts and stable renewal rates above 92%. In contrast, the Consumer Devices segment declined 8% in revenue due to softer discretionary spending and channel inventory corrections. Our Emerging Digital Platforms unit grew 18% year-over-year with a 24% contribution margin, though it currently represents only 14% of total operating income. Free cash flow for the trailing twelve months stands at $286M, down from $335M in the prior period due to higher interest expense and working capital absorption.

sections.heading: Strategic Reallocation Priorities
sections.body: Management proposes redirecting approximately $150M of planned capital expenditures from legacy hardware upgrades toward scaling subscription-based analytics and cloud-managed services. This shift is expected to increase recurring revenue mix from 48% to 61% by FY2028 and improve ROIC by an estimated 240 basis points. We also intend to pause expansion into two lower-margin international retail markets, preserving an additional $35M in near-term cash. The objective is to concentrate resources on segments with structural growth tailwinds and pricing power.

sections.heading: Cost Structure and Liquidity Actions
sections.body: To safeguard near-term cash generation, we are initiating a $60M annualized cost optimization program focused on procurement consolidation, real estate rationalization, and selective workforce realignment. Net debt currently stands at 2.9x EBITDA; our target is to reduce this to 2.3x by the end of FY2027 through disciplined capex and at least $120M in debt repayment. No share repurchases are planned for the next four quarters. We maintain $540M in available liquidity, including undrawn revolver capacity, which we believe is sufficient under our base-case stress scenario.

sections.heading: Board Decisions Requested
sections.body: The Board is requested to endorse the proposed $150M capital reallocation plan and the suspension of expansion in the two identified retail markets. Approval is also sought for the revised capital allocation policy, increasing the minimum investment hurdle rate from 9% to 11% to reflect the higher cost of capital environment. Finally, management seeks authorization to evaluate strategic alternatives for the Consumer Devices segment, including potential divestiture or joint venture structures. These actions collectively position the company to defend cash flows while accelerating exposure to higher-growth, higher-return segments.

structure.full_text:
Board Strategy Briefing: Capital Reallocation and Cash Protection Plan
Ref: BSP-26-041 | Date: 4 May 2026 | From: Elena Marquez, Chief Strategy Officer | To: Board of Directors

Section Macroeconomic Environment Update
Global growth forecasts for FY2026 have been revised downward to 2.3%, with continued weakness in European industrial output and moderating demand in North America. Central bank policy rates remain elevated, with our weighted average borrowing cost increasing from 4.1% to 6.2% over the past eighteen months. Input cost inflation has moderated but remains above pre-2022 levels, particularly in logistics and skilled labor. These conditions necessitate a disciplined capital allocation framework prioritizing liquidity, margin resilience, and returns above our revised 11% hurdle rate.

Section Portfolio Performance Overview
Core Infrastructure Services delivered $412M in EBITDA for Q1 2026, up 3% year-over-year, supported by long-term contracts and stable renewal rates above 92%. In contrast, the Consumer Devices segment declined 8% in revenue due to softer discretionary spending and channel inventory corrections. Our Emerging Digital Platforms unit grew 18% year-over-year with a 24% contribution margin, though it currently represents only 14% of total operating income. Free cash flow for the trailing twelve months stands at $286M, down from $335M in the prior period due to higher interest expense and working capital absorption.

Section Strategic Reallocation Priorities
Management proposes redirecting approximately $150M of planned capital expenditures from legacy hardware upgrades toward scaling subscription-based analytics and cloud-managed services. This shift is expected to increase recurring revenue mix from 48% to 61% by FY2028 and improve ROIC by an estimated 240 basis points. We also intend to pause expansion into two lower-margin international retail markets, preserving an additional $35M in near-term cash. The objective is to concentrate resources on segments with structural growth tailwinds and pricing power.

Section Cost Structure and Liquidity Actions
To safeguard near-term cash generation, we are initiating a $60M annualized cost optimization program focused on procurement consolidation, real estate rationalization, and selective workforce realignment. Net debt currently stands at 2.9x EBITDA; our target is to reduce this to 2.3x by the end of FY2027 through disciplined capex and at least $120M in debt repayment. No share repurchases are planned for the next four quarters. We maintain $540M in available liquidity, including undrawn revolver capacity, which we believe is sufficient under our base-case stress scenario.

Section Board Decisions Requested
The Board is requested to endorse the proposed $150M capital reallocation plan and the suspension of expansion in the two identified retail markets. Approval is also sought for the revised capital allocation policy, increasing the minimum investment hurdle rate from 9% to 11% to reflect the higher cost of capital environment. Finally, management seeks authorization to evaluate strategic alternatives for the Consumer Devices segment, including potential divestiture or joint venture structures. These actions collectively position the company to defend cash flows while accelerating exposure to higher-growth, higher-return segments.

text_content: **Portfolio Performance, Strategic Options, and Board Decisions Requested for FY2026–FY2028**

YF2025 group revenue was $12.4B with adjusted EBITDA of $2.1B. This performance delivered an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 17.0%, drievn by stable core demand and targeted cost discipline across business unist. Segment-level contribution varied, with higher margin expansion in Services and copmression in legacy Product lines; work is underway to normalize reporting and validate sustainment of margins. Cash conversion remained tsrong, supporting deleveraging and allowing selective reinvestment. This baseline positions the organization to evaluate portfolio moves against profitability and liquidity metrics.

oPrtfolio ROIC in FY2025 was 11.8% versus a 10.1% FY2026 planning WACC. The 170 basis point spread indicates value creation but also highlights limited margin for error on new investments and M&A — projects must demonstrate IRR ocmfortably above the planning WACC with appropriate risk adjustments. Recommended actions include raising minimum hurdle rates for brownfield investments, applying stricter satge-gate criteria for transformational programs, and conducting post-investment reviews at 12 and 36 months to verify realized returns and inform futrue capital deployment decisions.

Three strategic options are under active consideration to lift portfolio returns toward a sustainable premium over the planning WACC: 1) accelerated divestiture of lo-wROIC legacy assets with redeployment to higher-growth Services and Software adjacencies; 2) targeted inorganic acquisitions to secure capabilities where entry barriers create long-term returns; and 3) intensive operational programs to extract margin and working capital improvements. Each option is being stress-tested against downside macro scenarios, liquidity constraints, and a sensitivity matrix showing IRR outcomes at WACC ±200bps and governance

Board endorsement is requested on 2026-06-20 to approve a $1.2B capital reallocation program for FY2026–FY2028. The request seeks approval of allocation bands, delegated execution authority to the CEO and CFO up to defined thresholds, and a quarterly reporting cadence to the Audit and Finance Committees on deployment and realized versus forecasted IRR. Approval will enable reallocation in Q1 F2Y026 subject to standard approvals and pre-defined stop-loss triggers. The Board is aksed to vote to endorse the program and associated governance framework.
